--- title: "Paste a Vega-Lite spec" description: "spec_from_vegalite() turns a Vega-Lite JSON spec into a vellumplot plot, which then renders, composes and becomes a widget like any other. spec_to_vegalite() goes back the other way." categories: [Backend, Interactive] image: figs/vegalite.png --- [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/) is the most widely used grammar of graphics written as data: a chart is a JSON document with a mark, encodings and scales. There are thousands of Vega-Lite specs in notebooks, dashboards and documentation, and language models write them readily. vellumplot is a grammar of graphics too, and its plots [are specs](spec-as-data.qmd) already, so moving between the two is a translation rather than a reimplementation. ## A spec from the Vega-Lite gallery This is the [simple bar chart](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/bar.html) from the Vega-Lite examples, pasted unchanged. Its data is inline, so the JSON is the whole chart. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bar_spec <- '{ "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json", "description": "A simple bar chart with embedded data.", "data": { "values": [ {"a": "A", "b": 28}, {"a": "B", "b": 55}, {"a": "C", "b": 43}, {"a": "D", "b": 91}, {"a": "E", "b": 81}, {"a": "F", "b": 53}, {"a": "G", "b": 19}, {"a": "H", "b": 87}, {"a": "I", "b": 52} ] }, "mark": "bar", "encoding": { "x": {"field": "a", "type": "nominal", "axis": {"labelAngle": 0}}, "y": {"field": "b", "type": "quantitative"} } }' bars <- spec_from_vegalite(bar_spec) summary(bars) ``` ::: `spec_from_vegalite()` returns an ordinary `PlotSpec`: one `mark_bar()` layer, the inline values as its data, a discrete x and a continuous y. It renders like any other plot. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figs/vegalite-bar.png){fig-alt='Bar chart of nine categories A to I with heights from 19 to 91, converted from the Vega-Lite simple bar chart example' width=100%} ::: ::: ## External data, supplied from R Most real specs point at a file: `"data": {"url": "data/penguins.json"}`. `spec_from_vegalite()` does not download it. Pass the table you already have as `data =`, with the column names the spec uses. Here the Palmer Penguins get the names of the [vega-datasets](https://github.com/vega/vega-datasets) copy, and the spec is a scatter in the style of the Vega-Lite gallery. The spec's `"scale": {"zero": false}` keeps both axes on the range of the data, which is where vellum puts them anyway, and its `tooltip` channel becomes the layer's `tooltip`, so hovering a point in the widget below names its island. Anything the translation cannot carry over is reported, not dropped in silence. The `href` channel, a link behind every point, has no vellumplot counterpart, and the warning says so: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pen <- palmerpenguins::penguins pen <- as.data.frame(pen[complete.cases(pen), ]) names(pen) <- c("Species", "Island", "Beak Length (mm)", "Beak Depth (mm)", "Flipper Length (mm)", "Body Mass (g)", "Sex", "Year") scatter_spec <- '{ "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json", "data": {"url": "data/penguins.json"}, "mark": "point", "encoding": { "x": {"field": "Flipper Length (mm)", "type": "quantitative", "scale": {"zero": false}}, "y": {"field": "Body Mass (g)", "type": "quantitative", "scale": {"zero": false}}, "color": {"field": "Species", "type": "nominal"}, "shape": {"field": "Species", "type": "nominal"}, "tooltip": {"field": "Island", "type": "nominal"}, "href": {"value": "https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/"} } }' penguins <- spec_from_vegalite(scatter_spec, data = pen) #> Warning: Vega-Lite import dropped 1 unsupported feature: #> ✖ channel 'href' ``` ::: ## Now it is a vellum plot Once imported, the spec takes the rest of the grammar. Pipe on a theme and labels, and it is a widget with one more call: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins <- penguins |> labs(title = "Penguins, from a Vega-Lite spec") |> theme_minimal() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> as_widget(height = 400) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Hover a point for its island, click a species in the legend, drag to brush, scroll to zoom. The widget hosts the scene vellum solved; no Vega runtime is involved. ## The round trip `spec_to_vegalite()` translates the other way, for handing a vellum plot to a Vega-Lite tool. Inline data comes along as `values`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vl <- spec_to_vegalite(bars) str(vl[c("mark", "encoding")], max.level = 3) #> List of 2 #> $ mark :List of 1 #> ..$ type: chr "bar" #> $ encoding:List of 2 #> ..$ x:List of 2 #> .. ..$ field: chr "a" #> .. ..$ type : chr "nominal" #> ..$ y:List of 2 #> .. ..$ field: chr "b" #> .. ..$ type : chr "quantitative" ``` ::: The penguins go back out with their tooltip, and with `"zero": false` on both axes: vellum frames a scatter on its data, while Vega-Lite starts a quantitative axis at zero unless told otherwise, so the export says so. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} str(spec_to_vegalite(penguins)$encoding[c("x", "y", "tooltip")]) #> List of 3 #> $ x :List of 3 #> ..$ field: chr "Flipper Length (mm)" #> ..$ type : chr "quantitative" #> ..$ scale:List of 1 #> .. ..$ zero: logi FALSE #> $ y :List of 3 #> ..$ field: chr "Body Mass (g)" #> ..$ type : chr "quantitative" #> ..$ scale:List of 1 #> .. ..$ zero: logi FALSE #> $ tooltip:List of 1 #> ..$ field: chr "Island" ``` ::: The two grammars overlap for the common cases: marks, encodings, scale domains and types, binning and counting, faceting, inline data and titles. Outside that subset (polar coordinates, layer effects, patterns, statistical marks Vega-Lite does not have), both directions report what they left out. ## Specs from a model Because a Vega-Lite spec is just JSON, it is also what a language model will often give you when asked for a chart. The import above is one way in. The other is to let the model write vellumplot's own spec format directly: `vplot_ask(prompt, data, responder)` sends the model the JSON schema, the real column names from `spec_fields()` and your request, and validates what comes back with `vplot_from_spec()`. `responder` is any function from payload to JSON, so it can wrap any model API. The [agent specs page](agent-specs.qmd) walks through that loop, including the MCP server that exposes it to agents.
